topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing and pedagogical aims for the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional modalities of cancer treatment alongside the mechanisms, toxicities, and drug efflux pathways associated with non-targeted interventions.

topics.label: Exploiting tumor-specific defects and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies designed to exploit intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities such as hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint failure, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and resistance dynamics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the inhibition of oncogenic kinase signaling and examine the molecular adaptations that lead to drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-based targeted therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates selectively direct cytotoxic effects to tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immune surveillance and checkpoint blockade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for natural anti-tumor immunity and the application of checkpoint inhibitors to reawaken neoantigen-reactive T cells.

topics.label: Engineered T-cell immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss advanced immunotherapeutic strategies that physically engage or genetically reprogram T cells to destroy cancer cells.

topics.label: Clinical progress, challenges, and future paradigms in cancer care
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate overarching trends in cancer survival, systemic hurdles in therapy optimization, and future directions in patient management.
